title.narrative: UNDP Basket Fund ''Fostering Peaceful, Credible and Inclusive Elections in Sierra Leone 2022-2023''

description.narrative: The UNDP basket fund has been put together to support the elections 2023. In particular the project will enhance the capacity of the institutions responsible for the organization of electios in Sierra Leone, such as the Electoral Commission of Sierra Leone (ECLS), the Political Party Registration Commission (PPRC), the Judiciary and the Security Sector, to enhance crediblity and trust in the electoral process. It also aims to enhance transparency and inclusion by promoting citizen engagement, information sharing and information integrity by working with a range of stakeholders, including the Independent Commissions and CSOs.

title.narrative: OUTCOME 1 CAPACITYInstitutional capacity of electoral stakeholders is enhanced

description.narrative: I. In order to strengthen institutional and human resource capacity for a successful implementation of electoral process, the Elections ProjectProvided technical support to help ECSL strengthen its systems, processes and capacities for the collection, analysis, and dissemination of gender and disability disaggregated data, starting with the 2022 voter registration process. Provided solar panel to power the ECSL HQ ICT Unit and Datacentre located in the ECSL warehouse (Wellington). Spported rehabilitation of ECSL IT Server and generator rooms as well as warehouse roof and floor slabs. Delivered office and internet connectivity equipment to the PPRC headquarters and regional offices, an allterrain vehicle to support field missions, and helped upgrade its 75person capacity conference hall.Facilitated the visit of a PPRC delegation (the Chairman, two Commissioners and three Directors) to the Gambia to study the countrys experience in facilitating political dialogue and cooperation and strategies for promoting peaceful resolution of intra and inter party disputes. II In order to strengthen capacity to sustain a credible and accurate voter register and electoral process, the Elections ProjectDelivered equipment to enhance the operational capacity of ECSL for the 2022 voter registration process: mainly five heavyduty printers were handed over to the ECSL to produce voter registration lists for polling stations; one laptop, one printer and editing software were procured to strengthen the graphic design units capacity to produce public awareness material and a set of 18 generators and 18 printers was sent to ECSL district offices. III In order to strengthen Sierra Leones Electoral Dispute Resolution mechanisms to build credibility and trust in the electoral process, the Elections ProjectSupported the Judiciary to convene a group of experts to establish the Sierra Leones Judges Training Curriculum and the Compendium of Laws to improve the efficiency of the countrys Electoral Dispute Resolution Mechanism.Supported the Judiciarys training of 90 magistrates and court registrars, and the distribution of 1000 copies of Sierra Leones updated Compendium of Legislatives Acts to improve the countrys electoral dispute resolution mechanism.IV In order to enhance the capacity of the security sector, the Elections ProjectSupported the strengthening of technical and operational capacities of the Office of National Securitys Situation Room and the Integrated Elections Security Planning Committee through the secondment of two UN Senior Police Advisors; provision of ICT; the training of 600 senior security personnel on election security and conflict management; production of knowledge products and promotion of community reconciliation post the election. (Under UN Peacebuilding Fund)

title.narrative: Outcome 3: Inclusion in electoral processes is promoted and citizen engagement is strengthened

description.narrative: The Elections Project supported efforts for the increased visibility of voters from all walks of life including civil society groups, persons with disabilities, women, and youth.WomenWorking with UN Women, the Project facilitated the training of 90 aspirants and 260 female candidates from 14 political parties and supported the development of a common approach for candidates nomination process.In 2023, Sierra Leonean women represented 52% of registered voters, 36% of the candidates nominated, and 33% of candidates elected.YouthThe Project recorded considerable progress in youth engagement through the `Make Peace Win campaign led by the National Youth Commission. In May 2023, the Project provided technical support for NAYCOMs organization of Regional Youth Forums to identify strategies and activities to promote violencefree elections and active youth participation in the electoral process. The Project also supported NAYCOMs organization of a 3day National Youth Laboratory workshop, a platform used by UNDP for youth engagement in electoral processes, to encourage innovative ideas on youth participation in the electoral process and violencefree elections. The workshop awarded a 10,000 USD grant to five (5) regional youth networks for their innovative solutions. Persons with disablitiesThe Elections Project provided technical support for the adaptation of 128 polling stations to enable the access of persons with disabilities, as well as the design and distribution of 120,000 tactile ballot guides on average 8 per polling station to visually impaired voters.The Project provided technical support to the ECSL to establish Disability Stakeholders Coordination Groups in 11 districts across the five regions. Its joint efforts contributed to the a record registration of 22, 385 voters with disabilities.

The Project also supported NAYCOMs organization of a 3day National Youth Laboratory workshop, a platform used by UNDP for youth engagement in electoral processes, to encourage innovative ideas on youth participation in the electoral process and violencefree elections. The workshop awarded a 10,000 USD grant to five (5) regional youth networks for their innovative solutions. Persons with disablitiesThe Elections Project provided technical support for the adaptation of 128 polling stations to enable the access of persons with disabilities, as well as the design and distribution of 120,000 tactile ballot guides on average 8 per polling station to visually impaired voters.The Project provided technical support to the ECSL to establish Disability Stakeholders Coordination Groups in 11 districts across the five regions. Its joint efforts contributed to the a record registration of 22, 385 voters with disabilities.

description.narrative: The Project contributed to enhance the trust and confidence of stakeholders in the electoral process through outreach and strategic communication. I. Working with the Sierra Leone Association of Journalists (SLAJ), the Independent Radio Network (IRIN) and the BBC Media Action, the Project launched UNDPs iVerify solution on 5 April 2023 to proactively identify, monitor, factcheck and respond to misinformation, disinformation and hate speech during the elections. iVerify successfully processed 200 factchecking requests and left a positive mark on the countrys public discourse. The Project supported the redesign of the PPRC website and thereby helped improve its outreach efforts and promote the transparency of its operations.II Enhance transparency by strengthening the results management system. (Activity was not implemented due to ESCLs decline of the proposal to recruit a results management expert)III. Supported to the ECSL in the setup of a temporary election hub at the Bintumani Conference center and a permanent structure serving as a Media and Civic Education Centre (scheduled for completion in early 2024)
